status: research; nothing here is read by the build. Site figures computed on site/data.json of 2026-10-25 (round 47 live)
question: Can the buyer's share of Russia's exports be predicted (share model x Russia's no-war supply x no-war price) better than the current site rule?

rule.written: 2026-10-25, before any back-test result was computed
rule.candidate: SHR: no-war purchases(c,p,t) = Russia's no-war supply of p (back-test: Russia's total forecast at the origin, its log-linear trend over the ten years to the origin damped by 0.5) x predicted share(c,p,t). Share model: log share(t)/share(o) = b1*h*g_share + b2*h*g_demand + b3*dlog relprice(o->t) + infra(c,p,o,t); b1, b2 in [0,1], b3 in [-5,1], least squares without constant, pooled over buyers per product and data set, on M and L flows, y winsorised at +-1.5, trends at +-0.5 a year; fitted ONLY on pairs (o', o'+h) with o'+h <= origin (training from 1998, BACI 1995-2000 added for this); under 30 training pairs: prior b = (0.5, 0.5, 0)

drivers.g_share: slope of log share of Russia's exports of p over o-3..o (BACI: c's deflated value over Russia's deflated total; Eurostat: c's volume from Russia over Russia's total in BACI tonnes, or deflated value for gas)
drivers.g_demand: slope of log c's imports of p from all suppliers (Eurostat volume; BACI tonnes if the unit value is sane in every window year, else deflated value) minus slope of log world imports of p in tonnes, o-3..o
drivers.relprice: log(unit value of Russian p delivered to c / unit value of c's imports of p from all others), BACI; SHR uses the realised change o->t (known in the back-test, NOT in the war years: there it is held at the pre-war differential); SHR0 refits the model without it and holds it at the origin
drivers.infra: log(1 + sum over events known at the origin of net_factor x allocated capacity change o->t / c's volume from Russia at o), floored at log(0.1); events and net factors are in INFRA (1.0 for gas pipelines and LNG with named long-term buyers and no prior Russian flow on that route, 0.5 otherwise: new routes partly displace rail/sea flows, terminals run below nameplate); diffuse events allocated to the buyer group by imports of p from all suppliers at the origin
drivers.policy: EU diversification after 2014 and the Third Energy Package enter only through the infrastructure they financed (Klaipeda, Swinoujscie, Krk, Balticconnector, Baltic Pipe, IGB): a policy dummy cannot be estimated out of sample before 2014 (no pre-origin variation)
drivers.not_available: Urals-Brent and ESPO-Dubai differentials and route freight for 2001-2021 (Argus/Platts are paid; Minfin's Urals series and the IEA/OPEC pages refuse the connection from here): replaced by BACI unit values, which are near-FOB (BACI removes CIF margins), so freight is not in the price term

variants.SHR: judged model (owner's specification): supply forecast x share model with the realised price term
variants.SHR0: same without the price term (refitted): the version that can be applied in the war years
variants.SHRa / SHRa0: diagnostic: the share model x Russia's ACTUAL total (isolates the share part; used for the out-of-sample share-drift decomposition); never proposed

rule.reference: CUR, the current site rule (for M and L flows: origin year held flat; identical to M0 in these cells). Reported next to it: M0 (plain flat), D (round 48 demand model), SUP (round 49 supply model), as published
rule.error: the site's cumulative error: log(sum w*actual / sum w*predicted) over H = 1..5 years, w = 1 except 8/12 for the fifth year; per origin the mean over H1-H5 of the median absolute error
accept_if_all: accuracy: SHR's error at least 15% lower than CUR's at EVERY rolling origin 2005-2016 (12 origins, incl. 2008 and 2013/2014), at least 5 cases at each origin
band: SHR's era-calibrated 90% band for the five-year sum (H5; eras 2005-09, 2010-12, 2013-16; its own back-test errors) not wider in log width than CUR's

placebo: SHR's band, built only from earlier origins, covers at least 90% of the errors with the war moved to 2014 (origin 2013, H5; training origins up to 2008) and to 2018 (origin 2017, H4; up to 2013); under 10 placebo cases the product pooled over sizes

application consistency: because the war-time application cannot use the realised price term, a cell is proposed only if SHR0 passes the same three tests too; a cell where SHR passes and SHR0 fails is reported as 'passes only with information the war-time application cannot have' and not proposed
rule.scope: products crude (2709), oil products (2710), gas (2711; pipeline and LNG), coal (2701); size L (product flow over EUR 1bn a year, 4-year average to the origin; on Eurostat, as in rounds 48/49, the country total's size). Mid-size (M) cells of a product are judged under the rule only if that product's L cell passes on that data set; otherwise M results are diagnostic. Fuels are judged on Eurostat energy imports by country of origin for European reporters and on BACI elsewhere; a cell applies to a country only on the data set that covers it
rule.no_narrow_pass: a cell that fails narrowly fails; the rule is not changed after the results
rule.decomposition: share drift = log(share(t)/share(o)) of M and L flows, origins 2005-2016; explained out of sample = 1 - var(residual)/var(drift) and 1 - mean(residual^2)/mean(drift^2), residual = drift - predicted share change
rule.war_time: Russia's no-war supply index (2021 = 1, low / central / high, sources in SUPPLY) x the share factor exp(predicted share change) from the SHR0 fit at origin 2021 (drivers 2018-2021, price term 0, infrastructure planned before 2022: Power of Siberia contract ramp for China, Baltic Pipe for Poland, IGB for Bulgaria); gas split into pipeline and LNG with the site's own 2018-2021 mix; hubs (r48 list) keep the current method; the laundered line and re-exports are untouched; prices are the site's no-war paths (no windfall double count)
rule.bands: the site's cumulative band rescaled by the ratio of SHR0's back-tested country-total band to CUR's (per size class and horizon, as rounds 48/49), then widened by the supply range (low / high supply index)
rule.proposal: passing cells only, non-hub countries with purchases of EUR 0.1bn a year or more
rule.diagnostic: SHR0 on every in-scope cell (fuels, product flow L; and M only if L passes), non-hub countries

crude.basis: crude exports = output - refinery runs (runs flat at ~280 Mt). 2021: exports 231.6 Mt (customs), output 10.5 mb/d incl. condensate. OPEC+ (18 July 2021): +0.4 mb/d a month for the group from Aug 2021 to Sep 2022, Russia's baseline 11.0 -> 11.5 mb/d from May 2022, so Russia's required crude output rises ~0.9 mb/d from the 2021 average by Sep 2022. Energy Strategy 2035 (April 2020): output 11.15-11.25 mb/d to 2024, flat to falling to 2035. Low: output stuck at 2021 (capacity limits seen in late 2021). Central: half of the OPEC+ room is produced (about +0.45 mb/d, +4% output, +7-8% exports). High: OPEC+ path fully met, Strategy's upper bound

products.basis: refinery runs flat (~280 Mt, 2019-2021); the tax manoeuvre (2019-2024, law of Aug 2018) lowers the export of fuel oil while the damper and the 2011 modernisation agreements raise light products. Energy Strategy 2035: fuel exports 'rise considerably', fuel oil falls. Range around flat

coal.basis: Coal programme 2035 (government order 1582-r, 13 June 2020): exports 2035 +22% (conservative) to +86% (optimistic) on 2018 (bpb Russland-Analysen 386). 2018 210 Mt, 2021 ~223 Mt (BACI tonnes 222.5). From 2021 that is ~+1% a year (low) to ~+4% a year (high); the Eastern Polygon rail expansion (phase 2, 2019-2024) is the main constraint

gas_pipe.basis: pipeline gas to Europe and Turkey (Gazprom far abroad excluding China): 2021 ~175 bcm (185.1 incl. 10.4 to China). Gazprom's own 2021 guidance 175-183 bcm (April 2021). Low: 2021 level (spot sales held back in 2021). Central: 183 bcm (the top of Gazprom's 2021 target, demand-limited). High: 2019 level (~199 bcm) with Nord Stream 2 in service (the Nord Stream 2 range: on an origin basis it re-routes rather than adds; its value is the capacity to return to 2018-2019 volumes). China's pipeline gas is the Power of Siberia contract ramp (INFRA), not this index

lng.basis: 2021 LNG exports ~29.6 Mt (Yamal, Sakhalin-2, Vysotsk). Planned before 2022: Portovaya 1.5 Mt/y (2022); Arctic LNG 2, three 6.6 Mt/y trains in 2023, 2024, 2025 (Novatek, May 2021; half a year in the start year). Low: each train one year late. High: plus Yamal debottlenecking (+1 Mt/y)

supply_sources.what: OPEC+ 19th ONOMM, 18 July 2021: +0.4 mb/d a month from Aug 2021; baselines for Saudi Arabia and Russia 11.0 -> 11.5 mb/d from May 2022

Energy Strategy of Russia to 2035 (government order 1523-r, 9 June 2020; adopted April 2020): gas output 795-820 bcm (2024), LNG 46-65 Mt (2024), 80-140 Mt (2035); oil output ~11.15-11.25 mb/d to 2024
Coal programme to 2035 (government order 1582-r, 13 June 2020): output 485 (conservative) to 668 Mt (optimistic) in 2035; exports +22% to +86% on 2018
Power of Siberia: 10.39 bcm in 2021, ~15 bcm planned for 2022, 38 bcm/y design (contract 2014)
Arctic LNG 2: 3 x 6.6 Mt/y; Novatek (May 2021) trains in 2023, 2024, 2025
Gazprom far-abroad exports 185.1 bcm in 2021 (incl. China); 2021 Europe guidance 175-183 bcm
Russia's crude exports 2021, 231.6 Mt (Russia's customs report via UN Comtrade, HS 2709 net weight)
